run.procedureSummary: Five cycles, five steps in order, each step completed on all six crucibles before the next. (1) Charge: add the cycle's charge to each crucible; it may sit above capacity for now. (2) Overflow: walk 1 to 6; anything over capacity moves to the next crucible before that crucible is checked, and the crucible stays exactly full; overflow out of crucible 6 goes to slag (added to the loss tally). (3) State check on contents after overflow: BASE with contents >= upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; SUPERHEATED with contents <= lower mark becomes BASE; otherwise the state stays the same; at most one change per crucible per cycle. (4) Draw-off: work out all six amounts from the current contents first, rounding down. BASE sends floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED sends floor(q/2) to the previous crucible (crucible 1's half goes to slag). Then everything moves at once. A crucible pushed over capacity by returned melt stays over until the next cycle's overflow, or stays that way after cycle 5. (5) Global reset: if the total of all six is strictly above 38, each crucible becomes floor(q/2), the removed amount q - floor(q/2) goes to slag, and the cycle is noted; at 38 or below nothing happens. I used a short Python script for the arithmetic.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the emergency-tap halving: does the crucible keep floor(q/2), or is floor(q/2) the amount removed?
openPoints.assumption: The crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest, q - floor(q/2), goes to slag. This matters in cycles 1 and 4, where some contents were odd.

openPoints.point: Where overflow out of crucible 6 goes.
openPoints.assumption: It goes to the slag pit and counts in the loss tally (3 units in cycle 2, 3 in cycle 3, 8 in cycle 4).
The reset needs a total strictly above 38. The cycle 5 total is exactly 38, so there was no reset in cycle 5.
Both marks are inclusive: at or above the upper mark, and at or below the lower mark, as the write-up says. Example: crucible 3 at 4 with lower mark 4 went back to BASE in cycle 2.

openPoints.point: Melt returned in the draw-off that leaves a crucible over capacity.
openPoints.assumption: It is not trimmed in that cycle. The overflow is carried into the next cycle's step 2, and after cycle 5 it is left in place (crucible 2 ends at 10 against a capacity of 8).

openPoints.point: Whether a crucible's draw-off amount depends on melt arriving from its neighbour in the same draw-off.
openPoints.assumption: No. All amounts come from the contents before the draw-off and then move at the same time.
